summary: Set 133 Session 2 of 2, 'Confirm and correct the record' -- the terminal session of the release set. It runs after the operator published and ships no product code, by the spec's own Non-goals. CONFIRMED BOTH REGISTRIES, AGAINST THE REGISTRIES RATHER THAN THE WORKFLOW EXIT CODES, and the distinction turned out to matter. dabbler-ai-router 1.0.0 is live on PyPI (info.version 1.0.0; wheel and sdist both uploaded 2026-08-15T15:02:45Z). Extension 0.51.0 is live on the VS Code Marketplace (extensionquery returns DarndestDabbler.dabbler-ai-orchestration at 0.51.0, lastUpdated 15:09:32Z). Both tags resolve to the same commit 6f195bd8, with Test green on that commit (run 31891207265) BEFORE either publish workflow ran -- release.yml 31891571451, publish-vscode.yml 31891572217. OPEN VSX IS NOT PUBLISHED AND NEVER HAS BEEN. Its job is GREEN, and green there means skipped: OVSX_PAT is unset in the openvsx environment, so the step prints 'OVSX_PAT not configured ... skipping Open VSX publish' and exits 0 by design. open-vsx.org 404s on both the extension and the DarndestDabbler namespace. Checking that against history falsified a claim of the same class: the 0.45.0 row said it WAS published to Open VSX, and its own run log (29363250708) shows the identical skip. No version of this extension has ever reached Open VSX; both rows now say so, with the rule stated where it will be read next -- read a green Open VSX job as 'did not fail', never as 'published'. CORRECTED THE RELEASE-STATUS ROW, which had been wrong twice before (Set 112 S3 found it naming 0.33.0 live nine releases on; Set 107 S1 found it calling 0.46.0 staged after it shipped). It now states what is live with the run ids and tagged commit. Two further stale claims were fixed rather than left for a third occurrence: the router row still called Sets 105-116's work 'unpublished', and the version walk's 0.32.0 bullet still said 'not yet on PyPI' five weeks after it shipped. The walk gained an entry for this release. JOURNALED THE DELETION-COST RULING (authority=human, rubric_line=value-trade-off, verification_effect=none): a test whose only subject is deleted code is not a verification reduction, paired with extending 'no gate is added without deleting one' from gates to MODULES, and gated on the precondition that is the whole ruling -- the subject must actually be gone. The three cited module line counts were RE-DERIVED (contract_gate 1319, spec_admission 1082, replacement_gate 652) rather than inherited from the spec. It is a ruling, not an implementation: no code changed and no test was deleted. VERIFICATION HIT A PROVIDER OUTAGE, and that is the material fact of the session. Every OpenAI model on this seat returned 429 -- probed individually across gpt-5-6-sol, gpt-5-5, gpt-5-4 and gpt-5-6-luna, so account level, not one model and not a burst -- across three full attempts spanning ~20 minutes, two separated by a deliberate wait. With anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's own provider, google was the only reachable different-provider verifier, so the session took rung 2 of the documented escalation ladder. Stated plainly rather than buried: the verifier was gemini-pro at TIER 2 where the pinned verifier gpt-5-6-sol is tier 3, so the reviewing model was less capable than the pin. Nothing was skipped -- full scope, all severities, both discovery passes, both remediation-review cycles, every gate in force. Both decisions are journaled, the second SUPERSEDING the first rather than rewriting it, because the mechanism the first named turned out not to work. THREE TOOL GAPS FOUND BY HITTING THEM, all recorded as residuals and NOT fixed (release sets ship no product code): (1) verify_session hardcodes exclude_providers to the orchestrator's provider (verify_session.py:3345) with no flag to add a second, so the ladder rung it PRINTS in its own failure message has no mechanism behind it; (2) the more serious one -- providers.<id>.enabled is explicitly on the local-override allow-list in config.py and setting it to false changed NOTHING about model selection, so a control that loads, validates and reports as applied does not do what an operator reading that allow-list would believe; (3) the pre-close framing (verify_session.py:2823-2826) asserts change-log.md and the other close-out artifacts 'do not exist yet' rather than scoping their absence, so a terminal session that correctly writes change-log.md before verification hands the verifier a self-contradictory bundle -- which is exactly what happened. What actually reaches the fallback is clearing DABBLER_OPENAI_API_KEY for one process; the router consults key availability and says so in a clear note. Nothing persistent was changed. VERIFICATION OUTCOME: four rounds, gemini-pro throughout, anthropic excluded by model-registry lookup every round. Five Majors across the two discovery passes, then two more raised on the fix delta. THREE were false positives settled by deterministic evidence, never by the orchestrator's reasoning (C-003): the 134 directory attributed to this session has mtimes of 07:16, six hours before this session registered and five minutes before Session 1 did; change-log.md was reported as withheld from review while assemble_evidence shows it inlined at 11,217 chars; and ai-assignment.md plus the extra decisions.jsonl entries are mandated by the constitution, with Session 1's identical shape as precedent. TWO WERE RIGHT and were taken: a step-checklist post is missing for step 3, which is NOT retroactively fixable without writing a false record into the ledger the gate reads, so it is recorded rather than faked; and dist/extension.js.map was dirty -- from a pre-session rebuild (mtime 10:42:34, 2.5h before registration, with dist/extension.js byte-identical to committed) -- first justified in place, then REVERTED after round 3 rejected that fix, which was the better answer and available all along. ONE MAJOR SURVIVES AND IS DISPUTED, and the round budget is spent, so the operator adjudicates -- see blockers[0] and s2-remediation-round-4.md. In short: the finding's own acceptance criterion offers a change-log.md branch, that branch was taken, and the section is demonstrably PRESENT in the 65,219-char fix delta the round read. A third-provider opinion is unavailable because the outage that shaped this session removed the only remaining provider. TESTS, all three suites run AFTER the last change and green: pytest 4656 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed in 213s at -n 8 (the operator's 2026-08-10 cap, not pytest.ini's -n auto; identical specs and assertions). The single xfail is the deliberate strict-xfail pinning Session 1's open changelog.check() post-fold gap. mocha 1468 passing / 0 failing in 23s via the declared test:unit script. playwright 32 passed / 0 failed in 3.1m via the declared test:playwright command. NOT COMMITTED BY THIS SESSION, deliberately: docs/session-sets/134-ceremony-cost-and-what-to-cut/, authored out-of-band before Session 1 began and belonging to the next set. Its presence in the evidence bundle caused one of the false-positive Majors, which is itself a recorded residual -- an untracked directory belonging to a FUTURE set is indistinguishable, inside a bundle, from work the session under review produced. THE STEP-3.5 ANALYST EMITTED AN UNCALLABLE MODEL ID AGAIN ('claude-3-opus, latest version'), the fourth set running, despite a prompt that explicitly asked for a callable id or the provider and family only. It did caveat rather than assert this time. Its next-set recommendation -- 134-ceremony-cost-and-what-to-cut -- independently matches the spec already sitting untracked in the tree.
